contradictions.fact: Summit-day duration
contradictions.why: The day-2 schedule runs 4:00 AM to 6:30 PM (14.5 h) and reaches the summit block after 5.5 h, but the day's hours, the section breakdown and summitTimeHrs all say 11 h.

contradictions.fact: Hike-in time to Flapjack Lakes

claims.says: Most parties take five to seven hours in with climbing gear

contradictions.why: The camp card says 5-7 hours in while the itinerary and timing say 4.5 hours.

routes.name: Standard Scramble (Putvin Trail / Lake of the Angels approach)

contradictions.fact: Route distance

claims.says: Total round-trip stats commonly cited are roughly 9-12 miles

contradictions.why: dist_km 5.2 km (3.2 mi) is shorter than even the 3.5 mi to Lake of the Angels, while the itinerary (3.5 + 8.7 mi) and approach give ~9-12 mi round trip.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary, totalNote and approach agree on ~12 mi round trip; dist_km is the outlier

contradictions.fact: Gain from trailhead to Lake of the Angels

claims.says: about 3.5 miles and roughly 3,400 ft of gain from the trailhead
About 3.5 miles and 3,400 ft from the Putvin trailhead

contradictions.why: Day 1 gain of 2,900 ft is 500 ft short of the 3,400 ft every prose field gives for the same hike to the lake.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, pitch_detail, beta and bivy all say ~3,400 ft; itinerary day 1 is the outlier

contradictions.fact: Summit-push time
contradictions.why: summitTimeHrs holds the whole day-2 total (summit plus hike out) while the schedule reaches the summit 4.5 h after the 5:00 AM start.
contradictions.internal_resolution: schedule shows ~4.5 h to summit; 10 h is the whole day 2

contradictions.fact: Basin the Putvin Trail climbs through

claims.says: the trail breaks into the open, grassy Whitehorse Creek basin

contradictions.why: The route breakdown names a different creek basin for the same Putvin approach.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach and approach_variants agree on Whitehorse Creek

contradictions.fact: Permit note names another lake

claims.says: Upper Lena Lake is quota-limited, so book early

contradictions.why: The overnight-permit note for this route talks about Upper Lena Lake's quota, a camp this route never uses.
contradictions.internal_resolution: the route camps at Lake of the Angels (bivy, itinerary)

contradictions.fact: Rope length vs chimney rappel

claims.says: sling a chockstone/horn for a single ~120 ft (37 m) rappel

contradictions.why: A single 60 m rope rappels only 30 m doubled, so it cannot make the stated 37 m (120 ft) rappel of the chimney.

contradictions.fact: October in the climbing season

claims.says: typically safest to scramble July through September/October

contradictions.why: The season text calls the high country safest through September/October while the monthly guidance rates October risky and outside the window.
contradictions.internal_resolution: best_season, optimalWindow, climate and approach_variants all end the season in September; the season field's 'October' is the outlier

contradictions.fact: Early-season avalanche/wet-slide hazard

claims.says: postholing and wet-slide hazard are common on the approach
Lingering snowpack commonly covers the steep Sawtooth Pass slope

contradictions.why: The avalanche table marks June N/A while the climate text warns of common wet-slide hazard on the snow-covered approach in that season.

contradictions.fact: Whether a rope is carried

claims.says: a scramble with occasional roped steps

contradictions.why: The rope field says no rope while the gear list and protection text call for a rope on the steeper steps.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gear, pro_needs and detailed_rack all assume a rope for the steeper steps

contradictions.fact: Season window
contradictions.why: The season chip ends in October while best_season and the approach extend the window through November.

contradictions.why: The season chip ends in October while best_season and the approach extend the window through November.

contradictions.fact: Camping restriction names the other side of the range

claims.says: Camping on Snowgrass Flat itself is prohibited; use the sites below it.
there is no sensible way to reach either from the Snowgrass trailheads — the two approaches are separated by the whole crest

contradictions.why: The overnight-permit note gives the Snowgrass Flat camping rule for a route whose camp card says it is approached from Conrad Meadows, across the crest from Snowgrass.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, bivy and waypoints all use Conrad Meadows / South Fork Tieton; the Snowgrass note belongs to the west-side routes

contradictions.fact: Camping restriction names the other side of the range

claims.says: Camping on Snowgrass Flat itself is prohibited; use the sites below it.
there is no sensible way to reach either from the Snowgrass trailheads — the two approaches are separated by the whole crest

contradictions.why: The overnight-permit note gives the Snowgrass Flat camping rule for a route approached from Conrad Meadows on the other side of the crest.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, bivy and climbing_route all use Conrad Meadows; the Snowgrass note belongs to the west-side routes

contradictions.fact: Hardest grade (class 3 vs class 4)

claims.says: a safer Class 2-3 passage to the summit
A class 4 downclimb through the notch

contradictions.why: The header pill shows 4th class from rock_grade while the crux grade, the route breakdown, beta and descent call the finish class 2-3, and the approach variant and bail call the notch class 4.

contradictions.fact: Base camp elevation

claims.says: dropping a light camp in the upper Snowgrass basin around 7,100-7,200 ft
an upper Snowgrass basin camp (~7,100-7,200 ft)
the legal camping is in the timber and on the benches a little below it, around 6,000 to 6,300 feet

contradictions.why: The itinerary camps at 7,100-7,200 ft, practically at the 7,250 ft col, while the camp card puts the legal camps 1,000 ft lower at 6,000-6,300 ft.

contradictions.fact: Which side of Ives the route climbs

claims.says: Northwest ridge and upper south face of Ives Peak
follows the northwest ridge and a short south-face scramble to the summit

contradictions.why: The name and aspect say northeast slopes, but every route description climbs the northwest ridge and finishes on the south face.
contradictions.internal_resolution: face, beta, approach, climbing_route and waypoints all describe the NW ridge + south face; name/aspect are the outliers

contradictions.fact: When the access road opens

claims.says: the Snowgrass Flats approach road and upper basin are typically not fully snow-free until mid-to-late July
closed to wheeled vehicles ... roughly November-early June
gated and closed to wheeled vehicles each winter ... typically into early June

contradictions.why: The trip plan says the approach road is not snow-free until mid-to-late July while the road and access fields say it opens in early June.
contradictions.internal_resolution: road.seasonalGate and access.closures agree on early June

contradictions.fact: Route distance (one-way vs round trip)
contradictions.why: dist_km (7.1 mi, one-way to the summit) is shown in TECHNICAL STATS while the header distance is the 14.2 mi round-trip itinerary total.
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km is one-way; the itinerary is round trip

contradictions.fact: Which ridge of Old Snowy connects to the PCT

claims.says: up to the PCT and Old Snowy's north ridge ... downclimb the south ridge to the Old Snowy-Ives col
traverse back over to Old Snowy Mountain and descend its established south-ridge boot path to the PCT near the Packwood Glacier bench
reclimb Old Snowy's south ridge to close the loop over its summit

contradictions.why: The itinerary reaches Old Snowy from the PCT by its north ridge and uses the south ridge only to reach the col, while the descent text says the south-ridge boot path is what leads down to the PCT.

contradictions.fact: High camp elevation

claims.says: on the crest of Ptarmigan Ridge near 10,000 ft
establish a high camp (~10,300 ft) on the ridge crest
levels out at about 10,200 to 10,300 ft

contradictions.why: The camp card and route breakdown put high camp near 10,000 ft while the itinerary and both approach variants put it at 10,200-10,300 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary and both approach variants agree on 10,200-10,300 ft

contradictions.fact: Height of the summit bergschrund ice

claims.says: bergschrund navigation (25-30 feet of vertical ice)
Vertical ice pitches at bergschrund crossing (5-8 ft sections)
from a walk up a ramp to a short vertical ice step

contradictions.why: The route breakdown gives the bergschrund 25-30 ft of vertical ice while the watch-out list gives 5-8 ft sections for the same crossing.

contradictions.fact: Season window

claims.says: Early July into early August is the genuinely optimal window
Roughly Jun through Aug, best early July to early August

contradictions.why: The season chip and best_season start in July and run into September, while the seasonal guidance calls mid-June to August optimal and rates June good.

contradictions.fact: Summit-day timing

claims.says: aim to be on and off it by mid-morning
a pre-dawn summit push (~9 hrs round trip from high camp)

contradictions.why: The schedule reaches the summit in the late morning yet is back at camp 3,000+ ft lower by noon, contradicting the mid-morning turnaround; its 1:00 AM-noon camp-to-camp span (11 h) also disagrees with the ~9 h round trip in partner requirements.

contradictions.fact: Route distance (one-way vs round trip)
contradictions.why: dist_km (7.0 mi, one-way) is shown in TECHNICAL STATS while the header distance is the 14.1 mi round-trip itinerary total.
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km is one-way; the itinerary is round trip

contradictions.fact: Distance between Summerland and the trailhead

claims.says: A short, easy morning hike back down through Summerland and the forest to the trailhead.
reaching that popular alpine backcountry camp ... at about 4.5 miles
Continue to Summerland at about 4.5 miles
a little over four miles up the Wonderland Trail

contradictions.why: Day 3 hikes out from Summerland in 3.2 mi, but every approach field puts Summerland 4.5 mi from the trailhead (and day 1 reaches the higher Meany Crest camp in the same 4.5 mi).
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, approach_variants and bivy agree Summerland is ~4.5 mi in; 3.2 mi is the footlog crossing, not Summerland
